title: The Border of a Donation
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。一般原理を扱う架空の事例・論説。実際の組織、調査、実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Schools sometimes organize activities that provide resources to communities in other parts of the world.
sentences.ja: 学校は他地域のコミュニティーへ資源を提供する活動を企画することがある。

sentences.en: Students may understandably focus on the objects that can be collected, counted, and prepared for delivery.
sentences.ja: 生徒が収集・計数・配送準備できる物に集中するのは理解できる。

sentences.en: However, the usefulness of donated objects depends on circumstances that may not be visible to the people who originally selected them.
sentences.ja: しかし寄付物の有用性は当初選んだ人々に見えないかもしれない事情に依存する。

sentences.en: A donation is therefore not necessarily complete when the collected materials leave the school.
sentences.ja: したがって集めた教材が学校を出る時点で寄付が必ずしも完了するわけではない。

sentences.en: Imagine a student group planning to send educational books to a partner organization overseas.
sentences.ja: 海外の連携組織に教育用書籍を送る計画を立てる班を想像しよう。

sentences.en: The students initially select books that their own school no longer needs but that appear to be in good condition.
sentences.ja: 当初、生徒は自校では不要だが状態がよさそうな本を選ぶ。

sentences.en: A representative of the partner organization explains that the available storage space is limited and that some of the books may not match the languages or learning needs of the intended readers.
sentences.ja: 連携組織の代表者は利用可能な保管場所が限られ、一部の本は想定読者の言語や学習ニーズに合わない可能性があると説明する。

sentences.en: The students realize that sending a larger collection could create additional responsibilities for the people receiving it.
sentences.ja: 大きな集成を送ることで受け取る側に追加責任が生まれ得ると気づく。

sentences.en: They begin asking questions about the activities for which the materials would actually be used.
sentences.ja: 教材が実際に使われる活動について質問し始める。

sentences.en: The partner organization identifies several kinds of books that would support its planned lessons and explains why other materials would be difficult to incorporate.
sentences.ja: 連携組織は予定授業を支える数種の本を特定し、他教材を組み込むのが困難な理由を説明する。

sentences.en: Instead of attempting to maximize the total number of donated items, the students consider preparing a smaller selection that meets the identified requirements.
sentences.ja: 寄付品総数を最大化しようとするのでなく、特定された要件を満たすより小規模な選定を考える。

sentences.en: They also discuss who would be responsible for transportation, storage, and the distribution of the materials after their arrival.
sentences.ja: 輸送、保管、到着後の配布を誰が担当するかも話し合う。

sentences.en: The fictional example does not establish that sending books is the most effective form of assistance for any actual community.
sentences.ja: 架空例は書籍の送付が実際のいずれかの地域に最も効果的な援助形態だと確定しない。

sentences.en: In some circumstances, a different method of providing resources might be more appropriate, and the organizations involved would need to consider the relevant practical conditions.
sentences.ja: ある事情では別の資源提供方法が適切な場合があり、関係組織は関連実務条件を考慮する必要がある。

sentences.en: The important change in the students' project is the recognition that the recipient has knowledge that is necessary for evaluating the proposed assistance.
sentences.ja: 活動で重要な変化は受け手が提案された援助の評価に必要な知識を持つという認識だ。

sentences.en: The students begin to treat the partner organization's decisions as central to the project rather than merely requesting permission to deliver objects.
sentences.ja: 単に物の配送許可を求めるのではなく、連携組織の判断を中心として扱い始める。

sentences.en: International cooperation can involve the movement of resources across geographical boundaries, but that movement is only one part of a much larger process.
sentences.ja: 国際協力は地理的境界を越えた資源移動を伴う場合があるが、その移動ははるかに大きな過程の一部にすぎない。

sentences.en: A useful contribution depends on what people are able to do with the resources they receive.
sentences.ja: 有用な貢献は受け取る資源で人々が何をできるかに依存する。

sentences.en: Understanding those possibilities requires communication with the people whose activities the contribution is intended to support.
sentences.ja: その可能性の理解には貢献が支えようとする活動の当事者との意思疎通が必要だ。

sentences.en: The value of a donation cannot always be measured at the place from which it was sent.
sentences.ja: 寄付の価値は送り出した場所で常に測れるわけではない。

questions.prompt: Why is the departure of donated objects not necessarily the end of a donation?
options: Every donation must be returned to its source.
The school has no task before shipping.
The delivery location establishes their value immediately.
Their eventual usefulness depends on the recipients' circumstances.

questions.prompt: How do students initially choose books?
options: They follow a list of needs already provided by recipients.
They select unused books in apparently good condition.
They purchase only one kind of new book.
They send every book in their library.
questions.explanation_ja: 自校で不要で状態のよい本。

questions.prompt: What constraints does the representative mention?
options: Storage and the suitability of books for readers.
The students' examination schedule.
Only the age of the school's building.
The color and size of packages alone.

questions.prompt: Why can increasing the number of books be undesirable?
options: It guarantees that every student receives suitable material.
It always reduces storage requirements.
It may increase recipient work without meeting actual needs.
It prevents the organization from receiving any books.

questions.prompt: What does the partner organization identify?
options: The total number of schools in the world.
Book types that would support planned lessons.
The students' travel destinations.
The market value of all donated items.

questions.prompt: How do students change their goal?
options: They decide that the largest donation is always best.
They stop discussing the recipients' needs.
They require the organization to accept all materials.
They prioritize relevant materials over the total quantity.
Only the cost of school uniforms.
The creation of a universal curriculum.
Transportation, storage and distribution.
The selection of new teachers.

questions.prompt: What role does recipient knowledge play?
options: It helps determine whether the assistance is suitable.
It is relevant only after all decisions are made.
It replaces every practical assessment.
It proves book donations are always effective.
Types of printed materials.
Methods of storing books.
The total price of a donation.
Divisions or limits between areas.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Schools should avoid all international cooperation.
A large donation always produces a large benefit.
International donations should be designed around what recipients can use, rather than quantities collected by donors.
Receiving organizations should have no role in planning assistance.
questions.explanation_ja: 受け手の活用を中心に設計。

paraphrases.source: Instead of attempting to maximize the total number of donated items, the students consider preparing a smaller selection that meets the identified requirements.
paraphrases.rewrite: They consider a smaller relevant collection instead of maximizing quantity.

paraphrases.source: Understanding those possibilities requires communication with the people whose activities the contribution is intended to support.
paraphrases.rewrite: They need to communicate with the people whose work the donation should support.
